summary: PR #710 fixed the local/desktop path: sibling-tab retains wait on activeDetailLoaded, run in an idle slot and are staggered 100 ms apart, and the active thread is retained earlier (route loader). The gate is the weak part. It uses selectThreadDetailLoaded, which is also true for messages hydrated from a cache. The hosted browser persists the routed thread's messages locally (and the Hub thread read cache supplies them too), so on a hosted cold open of a previously opened thread the gate passes at mount, before any live window. The relay usually takes seconds to come up while the 6 staggered retains take about 600 ms. So all sibling retains are made before the relay can carry them, and their subscribeThreadWindow requests go out in one burst right behind the active thread's request: either via the watch()/register() loop or the transport flush on socket open. On the hosted path, the slowest one (E2EE relay), sibling windows therefore still compete with the active window, which is the cost the finding describes. Sidebar prewarm (3 windows, one idle callback, no gate, no stagger) has the same problem on a smaller scale. The optional smaller prewarm window was not done.

evidence.note: Effect gates on activeDetailLoaded, then startStaggeredThreadPrefetch (idle slot + 100 ms stagger, lines 70-106). This is correct when the gate means 'live window applied'.
activeThreadDetailLoaded = selectThreadDetailLoaded(store, activeThreadRef) for server threads; passed as activeDetailLoaded at 1226-1230.
selectThreadDetailLoaded is true when threadHistoryByThreadId OR messageIdsByThreadId has the thread. It does not exclude cachedMessageThreadIds.

hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache writes messageIdsByThreadId[id] (and marks cachedMessageThreadIds) for every cached thread with content, before any live window (3846-3850 does the same on the retainedLiveSnapshot path).
On hosted boot the local persisted read cache hydrates threads with record.content. The routed thread is kept with priority (527-539), so a reopened thread has cached messages at mount.
The Hub thread read cache also hydrates the routed thread's content before the node is live.
Elsewhere ChatView already treats detailLoaded as insufficient: the Claude review state requires activeThreadShellLive && activeThreadDetailLoaded, because cache-hydrated detail is not live.
retain(): attach() or, without a connection, watch(). Retains made before the hosted connection is up park here.
register() attaches every parked entry for the environment in one synchronous loop, so the stagger collapses into a burst (active first by insertion order, then all siblings).
Sidebar prewarm retains up to SIDEBAR_THREAD_PREWARM_LIMIT=3 (Sidebar.logic.ts:22) in one idle callback, with no active-window gate and no stagger. Same competition on a smaller scale.
Only the pure helpers are tested (stagger, cancel). No test covers the activeDetailLoaded gate or a cache-hydrated active thread.

remaining: (1) The gate useChatSessionTabsPrefetch.ts:130 relies on selectThreadDetailLoaded (storeSelectors.ts:178-185), which is satisfied by cache-hydrated messages (store.ts:3895-3912 via hostedHub/readCache.ts:286-297 and hostedHub/threadReadCache.ts:107-124). On a hosted cold open of a previously opened thread, sibling retains therefore start at mount, not after the live window. Because the relay is not up yet, they flush as one burst with the active request (supervision.ts:805-817 register loop, or the transport flush on open). Up to 6 sibling windows of 80-500 KB still compete with the active window over the E2EE relay. (2) useSidebarThreadPrewarm.ts:39-43 retains 3 windows in one idle callback, ungated and unstaggered, so it competes the same way at cold open. (3) Optional: no reduced prewarm window for speculative retains (MAX_SPECULATIVE_SIBLING_TAB_PREFETCH is still 6 full windows).
fixDefects: The gate in the implemented fix uses the wrong signal. selectThreadDetailLoaded counts cache-hydrated messages (cachedMessageThreadIds) as loaded, so in hosted mode the gate passes before the live window. The idle+stagger scheduling only spaces the retain() calls, not the wire requests: retains made before the connection registers or opens attach and flush together (supervision.ts:805-817). Minor: no hook-level test for the gate. The test's manual scheduleIdle cancel uses splice(indexOf(cb),1), which removes the wrong item if the callback already ran (test-only).
implementationSketch: S fix: (a) Add selectThreadLiveDetailLoaded(state, ref) in packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeSelectors.ts: threadHistoryByThreadId?.[id] !== undefined || (messageIdsByThreadId[id] !== undefined && !cachedMessageThreadIds?.[id]). syncServerThreadWindow writes the history entry, and writeThreadState clears the cached mark via markThreadMessagesLive, so both live paths flip it. Export it from @ryco/client-runtime/state/threads. (b) In ChatView.tsx (~1000), derive activeThreadLiveDetailLoaded from it (true for drafts) and pass it as activeDetailLoaded to useChatSessionTabsPrefetch. Optionally also use it in the Claude review check at ~4058 instead of shellLive && detailLoaded. (c) Move startStaggeredThreadPrefetch to a shared module (e.g. apps/web/src/lib/staggeredThreadPrefetch.ts). Make useSidebarThreadPrewarm take the same foreground-ready gate (e.g. the routed thread's live-detail state, or true when no thread route is active) and retain its additions through the staggered helper, not in one idle callback. Tests: selector unit tests (cache-hydrated content -> false; window snapshot applied -> true; legacy syncServerThreadDetail over cached content -> true). A hook test (vitest with fake timers, or a browser test) that a cache-hydrated active thread does not trigger sibling retains until syncServerThreadWindow is applied. A sidebar-prewarm browser test for gating and stagger. More robust M alternative, which also covers mobile and the register()/transport-flush burst: add a { speculative: true } retain option in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts. Speculative entries in an environment are not attached while a view-retained entry there is still awaiting its first live snapshot, then drain from a per-environment queue one attach per ~100 ms. Route sibling, sidebar and intent retains through it.
decisionReason: Client-side scheduling of speculative prefetch only. It does not change auth, E2EE, the Hub protocol or hosted lifecycle ownership: mutation readiness still follows the shell snapshot, and the prefetch was never a readiness signal.
